MINUTES
  REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  OCTOBER 16, 2017

A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 7:00 p.m. at the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR POPE.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those in attendance in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Giglia

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal, Persichina, Wroan

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director

4.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 18, 2017

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA,

  TO APPROVE THE  PARK  AND  ACTIVITIES  MEETING  MINUTES  OF
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2017.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he visited the site and stated that he agrees that this tree
  should be removed.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA,

  TO APPROVE THE REMOVAL OF THE CENTER CALIFORNIA PEPPER STREET
  TREE IN FRONT OF 4709 ROLLANDO DRIVE AND THE PURCHASE OF A
  REPLACEMENT STREET TREE AT THE COST OF THE APPLICANT AT 63
  ROLLINGWOOD DRIVE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. PVP LAND CONSERVANCY QUARTERLY REPORT

  Neil Uelman, Naturalist, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy, presented a report on the
  George F Canyon Nature Center for the months or May through September 2017.

  Mr. Uelman stated that there were a total of 712 adults and 343 children who visited the Nature
  Center. Hikes in the summer have increased, therefore, there will be additional hikes added to
  next summer’s calendar. The Scout programs and Library District programs are doing well.
  Docents have been added to the pool of volunteers.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA inquired about the attendance of the Full Moon walk and the
  Saturday walk. Mr. Uelman stated that attendance was okay and they will try to keep them
  towards the summer time.
   COMMISSIONER GIGLIA asked about the break-ins. Mr. Uelman stated that the alarm system
  has been put in, items are locked away, and the police report was filed.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI thanked Mr. Uelman for the report and asked if historical trend
  data can be provided for future reports. Mr. Uelman stated that this will be provided at future
  meetings.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PVP LAND CONSERVANCY QUARTERLY
  REPORT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  B. DAPPLEGRAY POA STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM PROJECT
  FUNDING REQUEST.

  This item is tabled to wait for one Commissioner to arrive in order to have a quorum for this
  item. (COMMISSIONER RETZ will need to recuse himself)

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A. ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA stated that the list of assigned parks is incorrect and should include
  the following revisions:

  Chandler Park/Pepperwood Park (Giglia)
  Silver Spur Park (Wroan)

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA stated that at Ernie Howlett Park, there are still two large trash bins on
  the trail from the Portuguese Bend show. Community Services Director Clark stated that he will
  look into this.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ commented on the June’s Trail construction and stated that at the
  bend it traditionally widened. Now it stays the same and he does not believe that a trailer would
  be able to get through. Community Services Director Clark stated that he will report this to
  Planning Director Wahba.

  Lisa Pierce, President, Dapplegray HOA, stated that the narrow trail issue has been brought up
  at DLPOA Board Meetings, but noted that a truck and horse trailer was recently able to get
  through.

  CHAIR POPE moved to receive and file the Adopt-A-Park Report.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA stated that at the Parade Subcommittee Meeting, the following items
  were covered.

    The Committee is still looking for a Grand Marshall; an invitation will be extended to
  Tracy Austin.
    The Community Grand Marshall will be Jackie Crawley, who was named Citizen of the
  Year by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce.
    The Ride with Santa Claus children’s representative will be the child of a daily shopper
  of the Promenade.
    The VIP seating area will be enforced.
    The Pre-parade event will be at El Pollo Inka at 4:00 p.m.
    The parade will begin at 6:00 p.m.
    The entrants who did not follow the rules in past parades will not participate this year.
    At the request of Deputy Bouse, the exit route will be changed.
    The Chamber of Commerce will be providing tote bags with merchant coupons.
    The Committee has agreed not to hold a November meeting unless an unforeseen issue
  arises.

  2
PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
MEETING MINUTES
OCTOBER 16, 2017
     The Park and Activities Commissioners will have a horse-drawn trolley.

  CHAIR POPE and COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that they could help with check- in for the
  parade.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

  A. ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION
  PROJECT REVISIONS.

  Community Services Director Clark provided the Park and Activities Commissioners with a copy
  of an e-mail sent by Susan Seamans regarding a change in the design of the Rolling Hills
  Country Club Estates Street Entryway which received approval under the Beautification Projects
  program. Community Services Director stated that he and Planning Director Wahba are working
  with the applicants on this project.
  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that since he was not present at the meeting when this was
  approved, he would like to have the opportunity to review the project and changes to the design.

  Community Services Director stated that the City Council has budgeted moving forward with the
  new Nature Center and the first step is demolition of the Community Center Building; is there
  any objection with moving forward with the demolition.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that this is a well-used parking area and suggested that signs
  be posted of the upcoming demolition work.

  The PARK AND ACTITIVITIES COMMISSIONERS agreed that there is not opposition to the
  demolition of the Community Center building with the recommendation to post signs to inform
  people of upcoming demolition work.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is interest from one of the Eagle Scouts to
  build a Little Library and asked the Park and Activities Commission with available locations.
  One location could be at the Nature Center.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested Dapplegray School. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  suggested Rancho Vista School.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA inquired about the Pony League. Community Services Director Clark
  stated that this will be on the future agenda.

  ITEM 7-B

  DAPPLEGRAY POA STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM PROJECT
  FUNDING REQUEST.

  Lisa Pierce, President, Dapplegray HOA, stated that she has a proposal pending with Bennett
  Landscaping and is not sure if it can be extended.

  Due to a lack of quorum, for this item, the PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSIONERS agreed
  to hear this item at the Joint City Council and Park and Activities Commission meeting on
  November 8, 2017.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  A. ADJOURN TO ADJOURNED JOINT CITY COUNCIL AND PARK AND ACITIVIES
  COMMISSION MEETING OF NOVEMBER 8, 2017.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA,

  TO ADJOURN TO THE ADJOURNED JOINT CITY COUNCIL AND PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING OF NOVEMBER 8, 2017.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  3

  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
